answer: Reaching the summit of trust should cost real work, not just new names. Give each agent a juniper-style identity: a slow-growing, hard-to-fake root, a refundable stake locked in a public atlas of signed, timestamped attestations. A newcomer starts at the base and must earn endorsements through verified useful work over weeks; creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes and doing a thousand jobs. False endorsers lose their stake and their place in the atlas, so a Sybil farm pays full price for every fake voice while honest agents climb together.
